identity.title: Position: Not All Explanations for Deep Learning Phenomena Are Equally Valuable

problem.claim: The paper addresses how deep-learning research should interpret and study surprising phenomena such as double descent, grokking, and the lottery ticket hypothesis.

gap.claim: The authors identify isolated, ad hoc explanations and argue that many prominent phenomena have little evidence of appearing in real-world applications, potentially limiting broader progress.

contributions.claim: Argues against treating deep-learning phenomena as isolated puzzles requiring bespoke explanations.
Recasts such phenomena as useful settings for refining broad explanatory theories of general deep-learning principles.
Proposes practical recommendations intended to align phenomenon research with broader pragmatic progress in deep learning.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors distinguish the value of phenomena research from solving each phenomenon as a standalone puzzle, emphasizing its role in developing broader theories.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report reinforcing their position by analyzing research outcomes from several prominent phenomena in recent literature.

narrative_sequence.summary: Deep-learning research has devoted substantial attention to surprising phenomena, including double descent, grokking, and the lottery ticket hypothesis.
The paper characterizes common explanations as ad hoc and case-specific, while questioning the real-world relevance of many prominent phenomena.
It argues that these phenomena should not be treated as isolated puzzles needing bespoke resolutions.
The authors retain their research value as settings for refining broad theories of deep-learning principles.
An analysis of literature outcomes supports practical recommendations for aligning this work with broader field progress.

source_observation.claim: The paper separates the value of studying a phenomenon from the value of explaining that phenomenon in isolation, favoring connections to broader principles.

lessons.interpretation: This framing can make a research question more consequential by clarifying its theoretical transfer beyond one observed effect.
lessons.application: When presenting a phenomenon study, explicitly state which general principle the case could refine and what broader understanding would transfer.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the research goal is deliberately narrow or when no defensible connection to a general principle is available.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the analyzed literature, concrete outcomes, detailed recommendations, or criteria for judging real-world occurrence or broader progress.
No comparative experimental results or independently verifiable theoretical results are provided.
